review: The hymn is Psalm 37:3–7 throughout, so the Hebrew follows the psalm: הִתְעַנֵּג עַל־יְהוָה (v4), הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל־יְהוָה דַּרְכֶּךָ (v5), וְהוּא יַעֲשֶׂה (v5), וְהוֹצִיא כָאוֹר צִדְקֶךָ (v6), קַוֵּה אֶל־יְהוָה (v7).
1:2 וְיִתֶּן־לְךָ מִשְׁאָלְךָ — the psalm has וְיִתֶּן־לְךָ מִשְׁאֲלֹת לִבֶּךָ; the short form is used so the line stays at nine syllables.
1:4 וְאַתָּה לֹא תִּיגָע — 'and you shall not grow weary', for وَأَنْتَ لَا تَتْعَب; the Arabic is a promise, and Hebrew keeps the imperfect of result.

4:4 וֶהְיֵה לוֹ סַבְלָן — 'and be patient for Him', for وَكُنْ لَهُ صَابِر; the noun סַבְלָן is post-biblical, but the piel סִבֵּל ('endure') is biblical (Isa 53:4) and the adjective is the shortest faithful option.
